fig1_data_fix.png.caption: Share of 3 s windows that contained no real packet (pure interpolation). A few corrupted timestamps stretched each recording 3-5x; after removing them before unwrapping, almost every window is real.

fig2_presence_groups.png.caption: Presence on every test group (standard preprocessing), same windows for every model, 5-window smoothing, thresholds chosen on validation. Shaded groups were part of V3's training data.

fig9_tradeoff.png.caption: Every possible threshold of the selected model: lower-left is better. The blue box is the provisional target (≤ 5 % false alarms and ≤ 15 % misses).

fig2b_presence_groups_robust.png.caption: Presence on every test group (robust_aug preprocessing), same windows for every model, 5-window smoothing, thresholds chosen on validation. Shaded groups were part of V3's training data.

fig3_loso.png.caption: Leave-one-source-out: V4 is trained on the other three sources and tested on the left-out one; threshold fixed at 0.5. Home and Office are the fair V3 vs V4 comparison.

fig4_noise_heatmap.png.caption: Each column adds one synthetic noise type to the raw test recordings (levels 1-3; 'crazy' = all at level 3). Darker = better. Noise is synthetic: this is a stress test, not real-world evidence.

fig5_noise_fa_miss.png.caption: False alarms and misses at the strongest level of each noise type; dashed lines are the targets.

fig6_gap_ablation.png.caption: Plain V3-style CNN vs the V4 gap-aware CNN, same data and training, clean and with packet loss.

fig7_counting.png.caption: WiCount people counting (standard pipeline), pooled over 3 folds (each window tested once). Counts 1-2: held-out recordings; counts 0 and 3: held-out time blocks of their single recording. Rows 4-5: no data exists.

fig8_counting_noise.png.caption: Exact-count accuracy on the same WiCount test windows when noise is added.
